items.title: You cannot occupy protest site for all time; what about livelihood of daily wagers? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that protestors cannot perpetually occupy a protest site, adding that such sites can be occupied only for a specified period to allow other groups to use them. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "You cannot occupy a site for all times to come. There are other protesters. Where will the farmers go? Where will the workers go? Where will the trade unions go? Where will the homeless go? Everybody has a right to protest," CJI Kant said. The Court also referred to the losses suffered by daily wagers because of the protests. "There are conflicting claims. The right to protest is also a constitutionally recognised right, as is the right to trade and carry on business. We are not talking about trade merely in terms of commercial establishments. We are talking about the source of livelihood of a daily-wage worker. Where does that person go for their daily bread?," CJI Kant said. items.title: Jantar Mantar should never have been a protest site; de-notified due to limited capacity: Delhi Police to Supreme Court
items.summary: Jantar Mantar is a public road and should never have been earmarked as a designated protest venue, the Delhi Police told the Supreme Court on Tuesday. In an affidavit filed before the Court by Delhi Police Commissioner (DCP) Anurag Kumar, it was stated that Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a protest site due to its limited capacity to accommodate large footfall, and its proximity to sensitive government institutions and embassies of foreign nations. The decision was taken by Kumar on the unanimous recommendation of a Ministry of Home Affairs committee, it was submitted. He termed the decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a administrative and executive decision. Further, nobody has the fundamental right to protest at a particular site, the affidavit added. The counter affidavit was filed in response to a petition by advocate Swaty Singh challenging the de-notification. Singh moved the Court contending that the move to de-notify Jantar Mantar violates the fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and to assemble peacefully under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. "The argument of the petitioner needs to be considered that in the flow of raising the slogans by mistake the words Zindabad has crept in instead of Murdhabad," the Court observed. A draft regulation is expected to be issued shortly for stakeholder consultation. The report was submitted pursuant to the Supreme Court’s directions to the Union government to conduct a comprehensive audit of the existing NEET admission system, identify gaps and recommend practical solutions. ACIT, New Delhi ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by the brothers challenging a 2019 Delhi High Court judgment that had upheld the Income Tax (IT) Department’s decision to reopen their assessments. The Court held that an investigation report pointing to the alleged overvaluation of shares constituted tangible material on the basis of which the Assessing Officer could form a reason to believe that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment. "The expression 'reason to believe' in Section 147 of the Act means cause or justification. Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Mohan Prabhu made the observation while rejecting a husband's contention that his wife was employed at a private company and therefore did not require financial support. The Court, however, found that the husband had failed to establish his wife's actual earnings. " The learned magistrate rightly held that the documents produced by the learned counsel for the respondent at the time of arguments cannot be relied, " the Court observed. It further held that even if the woman had secured employment, it would not necessarily establish that she earned enough to maintain herself and her minor child. The response has included the use of force by armed forces and law enforcement agencies, internet shutdowns, a paid PR campaign, censorship of social media content, and action against journalists and lawyers. A 12-hour Arunachal bandh was called by local bodies and youth groups, including the Siang Indigenous Farmers Forum (SIFF), Adi Baane Kebang United and the Adi Galo Welfare Society, on October 23. The bandh was followed by large-scale arson in Pasighat, East Siang district, targeting an office of the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC), a police station, and the homes of two MLAs and the BJP’s state president. The proposed SUMP, with an estimated capacity of 11,200 megawatts, is planned on the Siang River across the Upper Siang and Siang districts. items.title: Both Supreme Court and Manusmriti hold maintenance of wife to be pious obligation of husband: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently directed that enhanced maintenance be paid to a woman from her husband's salary, while referring to a Supreme Court ruling and a verse from the Manusmriti [Pinki Verma And Another v State of UP and Another] Justice Praveen Kumar Giri observed that both the top court and Manusmriti have held maintenance of wife to be a husband's pious obligation. "This Court observes that not only legal but a pious obligation is upon the husband to maintain his chaste wife, minor children and parents, if they are financially unable to maintain themselves. The same has also been observed in paragraph 10 of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Anju Garg and another vs. Deepak Kumar Garg, 2022 INSC 1033 : 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1314 , Section 125 Cr.P.C./144 BNSS as well as in Chapter XI Verse 10 (Ekadasha Adhyaya Shlok 10) of the Manusmriti," the Court said. The Court reproduced the Supreme Court findings, the legal provisions and the verse of Manusmriti in its order. items.title: Calling wife ‘stupid’, ‘useless’ not cruelty: Supreme Court quashes case against husband after her suicide
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday quashed a dowry death and cruelty case against a man whose wife died by suicide. The Court observed that allegations that he called her “stupid” and “useless”, even if true, do not constitute cruelty or criminal intimidation. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Manmohan set aside a Bombay High Court order refusing to quash the proceedings against the husband, finding no material establishing a nexus between the alleged harassment and his wife’s death. “The allegation that the appellant used to call the deceased ‘stupid’ and ‘useless,’ even if accepted prima facie, cannot to any extent qualify as an offence of cruelty or criminal intimidation. At best, it reflects on the temperament of the husband, but it cannot be given a criminal colour so grave as to become the reason for the suicide of his wife,” the Court observed. Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Manmohan The Bench also stressed that general allegations of harassment, without details of specific offending acts, were insufficient to continue criminal proceedings. The Commission held that charging for a carry bag would not constitute an unfair trade practice when customers were informed of its price and were free to decline the purchase. " It is also well settled that the shopkeeper is under no obligation to supply carry bags and that too, without any cost and there is no law which mandates providing free carry bag to the customer ," the Commission observed in its order of October 30. The dispute arose after the petitioner, Dr. Ramesh Singh Danu, purchased goods worth ₹1,435 from a Vishal Mega Mart outlet in Almora on January 18, 2023. items.title: Telangana woman allegedly beheaded by in-laws over land dispute
items.summary: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly beheaded by her in-laws over a property dispute in Telangana’s Mahbubnagar district on Monday, November 2. The accused allegedly attacked her with sharp-edged weapons after dragging her to their house, police said. The victim, K Sunitha, was a native of Obulayyapalli village in Mahbubnagar mandal. She is survived by two daughters, aged five and two. Her husband, K Balaram, reportedly has mental health issues. According to police, Sunitha was on her way to her agricultural field in Chinthal Thanda in Koilkonda mandal on Monday afternoon when her father-in-law, Manikya Naik, and her brothers-in-law, Manya Naik and Pandu Naik, along with Pandu’s wife, Parvathy, allegedly intercepted her. They tied a cloth around her neck and dragged her to their house, where they attacked her with knives and severed her head. Police suspect that the murder was premeditated. Police rushed to the spot after receiving information and shifted the body to the Mahbubnagar Government General Hospital for a postmortem examination. items.title: Call for Papers: NLUA Law Review Volume X - Submit by December 31
items.summary: National Law University Assam Law Review (NLUALR) is inviting submissions for its tenth volume. The NLUA Law Review is an annual, double-blind, peer-reviewed journal of the National Law University and Judicial Academy, Assam (NLUJAA). Special emphasis is placed on contemporary legal studies, along with the philosophical reasoning behind the law. The Journal, thus, aims to provide an opportunity to legal academia, research scholars, students, advocates, and activists working for the enhancement of the legal landscape through such scholarship. Submission Categories & Word Limits (Note: Word limits are inclusive of footnotes; a 10% relaxation may be permitted at the Editorial Board's discretion).
